title: Entropy-guided usage spike detector and automated mitigation playbook
creator: Marissa Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood Console ingestion shows frequent transient spikes in token usage and per-tenant latency. Traditional threshold-based detectors either miss long-tail distribution changes or trigger noisy alerts during expected diurnal patterns. This ticket implements an entropy-guided detection signal (distributional change in API path / model variant / token-rate vectors) combined with a constrained automated mitigation playbook for fast containment and low false-positive impact on customers.

Scope and goals:
- Build a streaming entropy scorer that runs per-tenant and per-route (route = model+API path) to detect distributional shifts in request characteristics (path mix, seq lengths, model variant usage, request burstiness).
- Correlate entropy changes with cost and p50/p95 latency deltas to reduce noisy alerts that aren't operationally meaningful.
- Provide tenant-aware suppression rules (min-volume, seasonality window) and a sliding stabilization window to avoid flare-ups.
- Implement an automated mitigation playbook that executes low-risk containment steps (adaptive throttles, non-critical job deferral, fallback to cheaper model variant) only when high-confidence signal + cost/latency degradation co-occur.
- Surface results in Console dashboards and wire up incident playbooks (PagerDuty + Slack) plus a one-click rollback in the Console.

Data sources and pipeline:
- Telemetry flows: edge -> Kafka -> Flink streaming aggregation -> ClickHouse (hourly/rollups) + hot aggregates in Redis for sub-minute detection.
- Features: per-tenant route histogram, token-per-request distribution, inter-arrival times, successful vs error rates, model-variant counts, cost-estimate per-request.
- Detector will be a Flink job that maintains compact sketches (count-min + entropy estimator) and emits events to the alerting topic.

Algorithm and heuristics:
- Use Shannon entropy over categorical vectors (route, variant) normalized by log(k) to get a bounded signal.
- Compute per-tenant baseline via exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) of entropy and a volatility estimate (EWMA of squared deviation).
- Trigger candidate when (entropy - baseline) > 3 * volatility and absolute token-rate is above tenant minimum volume (e.g., > 500 tokens/min).
- Validate candidate by checking concurrent p95 latency and cost-per-minute increase (relative > 15% above baseline) within a 5-minute window before escalating.
- Apply per-tenant suppression for seasonality hours (learned from 28-day medians) and temporary suppression for tenants with historically high false-positive rate.

Automated mitigation playbook (safe-first):
1) Post to #console-ops with summary and recommended action (manual by default).
2) If configured for automated response and high-confidence (entropy+cost+latency), execute step A then B with timeouts:
   A. Apply soft rate-limit (95th percentile throttling) for non-critical routes for 3 minutes and monitor effect.
   B. If cost/latency still worsening after 3m, automatically route new requests for low-priority routes to a cheaper compatible model variant and re-enable caching for repeated prefixes.
   C. If still degrading, enqueue an automated incident (PagerDuty), create Linear ticket template, and attach diagnostics snapshot.
3) All automated changes are tagged and auto-reverted after stabilization window (10 minutes) unless escalated.

Acceptance criteria (done = release-ready):
- Detector reduces false-positive rate by >= 40% vs baseline threshold detector on last 90 days of historical incidents (measured on labeled incident set).
- Mean time to detection (MTTD) improves to < 3 minutes for high-impact spikes in synthetic replay tests.
- Automated mitigation successfully reduces p95 latency by >= 20% in controlled canary runs without causing >2% additional 5xx errors.
- Dashboards: entropy signal, candidate events feed, mitigation actions, rollback actions available in Grafana.
- Runbook and playbook documented in Confluence and validated with on-call rotation.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement Flink job + unit tests and local harness. Target: PR by 2026-03-08.
- Phase 2 (canary): deploy detector in shared canary cluster for 10% of telemetry (sampling) and test mitigation in dry-run (no automation) for 1 week.
- Phase 3 (small-tenant auto): enable automation for low-risk tenant cohort (opt-in customers) for 2 weeks.
- Phase 4 (gradual expand): expand to higher-volume tenants with tuned suppression settings and SRE signoff.

Dashboards and artifacts:
- Detector Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/usage/entropy-spikes
- Confluence design and playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Entropy+Spike+Detector+Playbook
- PRs and code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pulls (see linked PR below)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Automated throttling could impact latency-sensitive customers. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, opt-in automation, immediate rollback tagging, and canary cohorts.
- Risk: Sketch-based estimators lose accuracy for very small cardinalities. Mitigation: fall back to raw counters for low-cardinality tenants.
- Risk: Detector adds CPU on streaming tier. Mitigation: offload heavy post-processing to aggregated batch jobs and rely on compact sketches in Flink.

Notes on observability and testing:
- Add event-level metadata to the alert topic so Console UI can show top contributing route/variant histograms and sample traces.
- Synthetic traffic generator to simulate varied distributional changes is included in the PR.

Deliverables:
- Flink job, unit + integration tests, Grafana panels, Confluence runbook, remediation task executor (+ feature flag), and one-click rollback button in Console.

Links (working artifacts):
- Design doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3782
- Synthetic replay harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/tree/main/synthetic-replay

Acceptance rubric and rollout sign-offs will be recorded in the PR and Confluence page.
